page: Microsoft Azure E64-32as_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine operating on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture with a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The configuration allocates 32 dedicated vCPUs derived from 16 physical cores via simultaneous multithreading, backed by 32 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial at 512.0 GB of RAM, providing 16.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. There is no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached remote storage, and no GPU hardware is present.

Benchmark evaluations reflect a balanced performance profile with notable strengths in memory throughput and single-threaded operations. The PassMark memory benchmark and stress-ng single-core CPU metrics rank in the top 25 percent tier, alongside strong results in Geekbench image processing and small-model LLM generation. Multi-core performance across stress-ng and PassMark aligns within the middle 50 percent range, as do Redis SET operations and data compression benchmarks. Processing large machine learning workloads like 70B models exhibits low throughput due to execution on general-purpose CPU cores without hardware acceleration.

The hardware configuration of 32 vCPUs coupled with 512 GB of RAM provides cost efficiencies for software licensed on a per-core basis that requires large memory pools. The absence of integrated local storage shifts all persistence and IOPS dependencies to external volumes. This instance is suited for enterprise relational database engines, high-capacity in-memory data stores such as Redis, data warehousing, and memory-bound ETL pipelines.
